C0.quote: We study how voting rules shape voter coordination in large threecandidate elections.
C0.note: Strategic/equilibrium analysis of Plurality, Anti-Plurality and Approval Voting.

C1.quote: We show that the Condorcet winner is always elected at some equilibrium under Approval Voting
C1.note: AX: Condorcet-consistency of rules at equilibrium; mainly EQ; WD (welfare guarantees); SI (Monte-Carlo of tâtonnement).

C2.1.quote: the set of messages (or ballots) available to each voter

C2.2.quote: Approval Voting is defined by M AV = {a, b, c, ab, ac, bc}
C2.2.note: Ballots are single or two-candidate approval sets (PL: one; APL: two); voters' held types are rankings plus cardinal utility.

C2.3.quote: A voter’s type t consists of his von Neumann and Morgenstern preference
C2.3.note: Types (ordinal and cardinal utilities) are held attitudes.

C2.4.quote: A (pure) strategy is a measurable function σ : T → M .
C2.4.note: Types T separate from ballots M; strategic voting and expressive voting discussed.

C3.1.quote: We consider in this section simulations where only a fraction of the electorate is strategic
C3.1.note: Main analyses are strategic; the expressive-voter robustness simulations include non-strategic voters (sincere ballots).

C3.2.quote: casting a ballot for the candidate they prefer, independently of her chance of winning
C3.2.note: Expressive voters are stated to vote their preferences.

C3.3.quote: in line with recent empirical studies (see Section 7)
C3.3.note: Expressive voting motivated by empirical literature on share of expressive voters; this is citing empirical studies, no argument by the paper itself; closest fit is CONV/EMP. CONV chosen as only citations.

C4.1.quote: he attaches utility 1 (resp. 0) to his preferred (resp. worst) candidate
C4.1.note: Utility of second-best candidate u in (0,1); ballot choice defined via utility threshold; ordinal type consistent with cardinal representation.

C5.1.quote: we consider an alternative welfare criterion, utilitarian welfare
C5.1.note: Also Rawlsian and anti-Rawlsian welfare, Propositions 4 and 6.

C5.2.quote: Wi = r i + r ki ∫ udF ki (u) + r ji ∫ udF ji (u)
C5.2.note: Welfare evaluated on held cardinal utilities of the type distribution, defined separately from ballots.

VOT.quote_behav: some voters vote expressively, casting a ballot for the candidate they prefer
VOT.quote_info: a fraction of voters updates its behavior after the publication
VOT.note: Strategic best replies in main analysis; expressive (non-strategic) voters in robustness. Info: beliefs on aggregate profile (Poisson common knowledge probabilities / polls).

DES.note: Rules are compared, but designer's choice not modelled.
